THE SPLANDOR OF NEBUCHADNEZZAR.

144800 - The ruins of the Temple of Esagila, probably the most importantAdditional sanctuary, which is supposed to have connected with the Tower of Babel and which may have been part of the supports of the famous Hanging Gardens, one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. Most of the temples were of but one story but at times they were pyramided on smaller and smaller foundations of sun dried brick. The plainness of the brick walls was relieved by stucco on which designs were painted.

THE SPLENDER OF NEBUCHADNEZZAR.

144712 - One of the places recently uncovered among the ruins og Babies. Here it is possible that the mighty Nebuchadnezzar II may have ruled. We know that it is a royal palace for this is shown by the lion which may be see in the middle distance, always a sign of royalty. It is unfortunate that a series of weak kings following Nebuchadnezzar allowed the city to be over-run by the wilder tribes of A&A Minor and many of its records destroyed. The palace, while of but one story, covered a great area and was a prize of corridors, passages and rooms.
